content: The test image shows a corn ear with white to grayish-white cottony mold growing between kernel rows in streaks/bands along the ear, yellow kernels with some discoloration, and dark brown rot at the tip. Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Diplodia**, **Fusarium**, and possibly **Ear_rots_Gibberella**.

## Analysis

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear with **yellow kernels** still largely intact (not shrunken or tan)
- **White to grayish-white cottony mold** growing in elongated streaks/bands between kernel rows along the ear's length
- **Dark brown tip rot** at the top of the ear
- Husk partially peeled back, revealing patchy white mold distribution

**Candidate comparison:**

| Disease | Key feature | Match? |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| **Fusarium** | White/pinkish mold patches on yellow kernels, patchy clusters | ✅ Strong match |
| Ear_rots_Diplodia | White mold but kernels become tan/brown and shrunken | ❌ Kernels are yellow, not tan |
| Ear_rots_Gibberella | Pink/red mold starting at tip | ❌ No pink/red mold visible |
| Ear_rots_Trichoderma | Blue-green mold | ❌ Mold is white, not blue-green |
| Ear_rots_Aspergillus | Olive-green dusty mold | ❌ Mold is white, not olive-green |

**Key differentiators:** The yellow kernel color clearly rules out Diplodia (which produces tan/brown shrunken kernels). The white cottony mold growing between kernel rows in patchy/streaky clusters on an otherwise yellow ear is the hallmark of Fusarium ear rot, consistent with the description of "white-to-pinkish cottony mycelial growth appearing between and around individual kernels, forming irregular, patchy clusters rather than a uniform coating."
